assessments.reasoning: GNU 1.3 [17885,18530) contains both automatic termination and the holder-specific cessation rule. Its two reinstatement clauses distinguish provisional status from the permanent effect of a holder’s failure to notify in time.

challenge.method: Compared cessation with receipt as possible starting events. Tested reasonable notification by the same holder just before and exactly at the 60-day threshold, and notification by a different holder.
challenge.results: Cessation starts this clock. Notification just before the threshold defeats the no-timely-notification condition. Notification exactly at the threshold falls outside the specified period. Another holder’s notification cannot satisfy this holder’s condition. Timely notification alone does not constitute explicit final termination. The separate first-notice cure route remains relevant on its own terms.

limitations: Actual cessation of all violations, the identity of the holder, reasonable notification and explicit final termination each require separate facts.
reasoning: Under 1.3 §9, an unauthorized attempt to exercise one of the listed rights is void and automatically terminates the licensee’s rights. Once all violations of the license cease, the license from each particular holder is provisionally reinstated unless and until that holder explicitly and finally terminates it. Permanent reinstatement under the cessation provision depends on whether that holder gave reasonable notification before the 60-day threshold.
